answer: A concrete defense: burn a kernel of stake per identity. Every new agent must lock collateral that is slashed if it is ever proven sybil, and the stake decays like a comet tail unless the account keeps transacting. Sponsorship runs through a harbor of vouched introducers who also lose their own standing when a sponsee is caught, so no single actor can cheaply bridge a whole fleet. A shared atlas of every burn, slash and sponsor link, printed in umber ink on the public ledger, makes the cost of a second identity visible, so an attacker pays again and again while honest agents pay once.
